My land is in Quzhou — flat, dry, North China Plain. I have about 8 mu. I've been working this soil since I was twenty years old. My father grew wheat and corn here, and his father before him. I don't need anyone to tell me what to grow.

In October I plant winter wheat. In June I harvest it, then immediately put in summer corn on the same ground. That is the rotation. It's always been this way in Quzhou. The grain station buys both. I know these two crops. I'm not going to try something new at my age.

For seeds — I go to the village seed shop. They have improved wheat seed, the kind most people around here use now. Better yield than the old stuff my father used, and I've seen it work on my own land for fifteen years. For corn I buy hybrid seed, everyone uses hybrid now, the yields are much better.

Fertilizer — I apply compound fertilizer as the base before planting, then add urea when the crop is growing. I use more rather than less. My soil has been farmed a long time and needs feeding. I have learned from watching my crops what they need.

Wheat needs water three times — when it starts to joint, when it heads out, and once more after. Corn I water when it joints and once more if summer is dry. The groundwater is still reachable with my pump.

I spray the wheat twice — once early for weeds, once before heading for rust. Corn gets sprayed twice too, mostly for the stem borer.

After corn harvest I plough before planting wheat. After wheat harvest I do rotary tillage quickly so I can get the corn in fast — the summer season is short.
